newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes steady, ADNOC differential weakens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes steady, ADNOC differential weakens.

text.p: The light Middle East crude market started July trading with Qatar land and Murban deals heard done.
A shosha heard sold the first July cargo of Qatar Land, to a South Korean refiner at QGPC even.
The price was higher than the last June Qatar Land trade, which was at QGPC -10. But the July cargo was heard to be in exchange for July Oman, which would affect outright levels.
A South Korean refiner was also rumoured to have sold July Murban to a major at ADNOC -28, lower than earlier market expectations that July trading would start at ADNOC -10/15.

But Oman trading was lacklustre, keeping traders uncertain where to peg realistic market levels. Traders expected a clearer idea of Oman price on an MPM basis to emerge following the results of the Bangchak tender, which closes tomorrow.
The only July trade done recently was a partial cargo widely heard done between two majors at Dubai +67.
But the level was considered low by some traders, who thought that it was meant to give an idea to MPM of the weakness of the spot Oman market.
The MPM retroactive official price for May Oman is due out next week.
On Asian crudes, July Bach Ho was heard sold to China at OSP +40. The level surprised many traders who did not expect Bach Ho premiums to be as high.
With Bach Ho OSP currently at Minas +80, this would put the absolute price of Bach Ho almost equal to the Minas level, making Minas more competitive.
The Duri market was also firm, as a shortage of June spot supplies underpins premiums. Duri sellers were holding out for ICP +30, compared to the ICP -25 traded in May.
